Matta Nishanth Nimshi Boon, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh,
on 18 December, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Mallikarjuna Rao
 Criminal Petition No.9370 of 2023
O R D E R:

entities.text: Matta Nishanth Nimshi Boon, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1. Under section 438 of Cr.P.C., this Criminal Petition has been filed by the Petitioner/Accused No.1,
seeking anticipatory bail, in Crime No.491 of 2023 of Eluru III Town Police Station, Eluru District.

entities.text: Eluru III Town Police Station, Eluru District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. A case has been registered against the Petitioner for the offences punishable under Section 417,
420, 493 r/w 34 of IPC.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the Victim-cum-Defacto Complainant by name Karnulu Santhi was studying B.Tech 2nd year in the CSE Branch at Sri C.R.Reddy College, Eluru by staying in the C.R.Reddy Pharmacy Hostel, Eluru and while so, the Defacto Complainant got acquaintance with A.1, who studied in the same college through one Uttu Bhai, and the Defacto Complainant and A.1 exchanged their phone numbers and used to talk with each other and later it was turned into love.
On 26.06.2023, A.1 went to the college and in the break time i.e., at about 10.40 AM, he took the victim to his house and introduced her to his mother (A.2), uncle (A.3) and sister (A.4) and they all promised that they would perform the A.1's marriage with her and informed them that they would live free with each other and later they all went out from the house and later in the absence of inmates, A.1, on the pretext of marriage, had sexual intercourse with her against her will, and since then, he had enjoyed her sexually on several occasions, and later, he refused to marry her.
4. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits the Petitioner is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case; no prima facie case is made out against the Petitioner for the alleged offences levelled against him; he did not cohabitate deceitfully with the Defacto Complainant and induced a belief of lawful marriage; he is an Engineering student; if he is arrested, it will adversely affect his educational career and future life; there is no question of his absconding or tampering with the evidence and the entire investigation has been completed; the other accused were already granted anticipatory bail by the learned Sessions Judge, Eluru, by its order dated 04.11.2023 in Crl.M.P.Nos.1024 of 2023 and 1025 of 2023.
5.
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the grant of bail on the ground that the investigation was pending.
6. I have heard both sides.
Perused the record.
7. The material on record indicates that the crime is registered against the Petitioner/Accused and others for the offences punishable under sections 417, 420, 493 r/w 34 of IPC.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner contends the offences under sections 417 and 420 of IPC are offences punishable up to Matta Nishanth Nimshi Boon, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48943954/
1 7 years and the Petitioner is entitled to the benefit of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar and another1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as the offence alleged against the Petitioner under section 493 of IPC is concerned, the ingredients of section 493 of IPC will not be attracted to the facts of the case.

8. The essence of the section is therefore the deception caused by a man on a woman, in consequence of which, she is led to believe that she is lawfully married to him while, in fact, they are not lawfully married.
To establish deception, there must first be allegations that the accused falsely induced her to believe that she is legally wedded to him.
As seen from the report, there is no allegation of any such deception or inducement.

Even according to the Defacto Complainant, she and Petitioner fully knew that they were not husband and wife and that no ceremony of marriage took place between them, there is no question of one of them believing otherwise.
Even if the entire allegations in the report are taken as true, the section is not being attracted.
What is alleged in the report is only a promise to marry in future.
Thus, the facts prima facie cannot at any rate attract section 493 of IPC.

I do find force in the submission of the learned counsel for the Petitioner,
though, the Petitioner placed reliance on the decisions in Suram Kiran Kumar Reddy and others V.
State of A.P., and another2 and Moideenkutty Haji and others V. Kunhikoya and others3.
9.

sentences.text: While advancing arguments in Crl.M.P.No.1061 of 2023 seeking bail, the I Additional District and District Sessions Judge, West Godavari, Eluru, has (2014) 8 SCC 273 2002 (6) ALT 565 AIR 1987 Kerala 184 not followed the principles laid down in those decisions by giving its own reasons.

entities.text: I Additional District and District Sessions Judge, West Godavari, Eluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: A reading of the Order in Crl.M.P.No.1061 of 2023 shows that the learned Judge observed that the investigation is at the threshold and the criminal acts made by the Petitioner even against the victim whether would fall under section 376 of IPC or not, has to be thoroughly investigated by the Investigation officer.

10. Learned counsel for the Petitioner contends that as seen from the report of the Victim, the ingredients of section 376 of IPC are not attracted, as such, the crime is not registered under section 376 of IPC against the Petitioner.
To consider the said submission, I have carefully gone through the report lodged by the victim girl.

11. In Pramod Suryabhan Pawar V. State of Maharashtra and another4, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that:
16. Where the promise to marry is false and the intention of the maker at the time of making the promise itself was not to abide by it but to deceive the woman to convince her to engage in sexual relations, there is a "misconception of fact" that vitiates the woman's "consent".

entities.text: Pramod Suryabhan Pawar V. State of Maharashtra and another4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, a breach of a promise cannot be said to be a false promise.
To establish a false promise, the maker of the promise should have had no intention of upholding his word at the time of giving it.
The "consent" of a woman under Section 375 is vitiated on the ground of a "misconception of fact" where such misconception was the basis for her choosing to engage in the said act.
(2019) 9 SCC 608 xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx Matta Nishanth Nimshi Boon, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48943954/

entities.text: Matta Nishanth Nimshi Boon, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To summarise the legal position that emerges from the above cases, the "consent" of a woman with respect to Section 375 must involve an active and reasoned deliberation towards the proposed act.
To establish whether the "consent" was vitiated by a "misconception of fact" arising out of a promise to marry, two propositions must be established.
The promise of marriage must have been a false promise, given in bad faith and with no intention of being adhered to at the time it was given.
The false promise itself must be of immediate relevance, or bear a direct nexus to the woman's decision to engage in the sexual act.

12. The legal position which can be culled out from the judicial pronouncements referred to above is that if a man retracts his promise to marry a woman, consensual sex they had will not constitute an offence of rape under Section 376 of the IPC, unless it is established that the consent for such sexual act was obtained by him by giving false promise of marriage with no intention of being adhered to and that promise made was false to his knowledge.
13. The report does not disclose that the Petitioner/Accused had no intention to marry the Victim at the very inception.
It is also not referred in the report that the Petitioner made a false promise.

Even otherwise, the investigation discloses that the Petitioner/Accused alleged to have committed the offence punishable under section 376 of IPC, the law will take its own course to deal with a situation.
To consider the anticipatory bail application, the Court must go through the contents of the report and other material placed on record.
Such relief cannot be denied in anticipation that the investigation is to be carried out whether the ingredients of section 376 of IPC would attract or not.

14. Given the aforesaid circumstances, this Court views that the facts prima facie cannot attract section 493 of IPC and since the offences alleged under sections 417 and 420 of IPC are punishable with imprisonment of up to seven years, this Court directs the Police to follow the procedure as contemplated under Section 41A of Cr.P.C., scrupulously as per the guidelines enunciated in Arnesh Kumar case referred to supra.
15.

Nothing stated above shall be construed as a final expression of opinion on the merits of the case,
and the trial will proceed independently of the observations made in the present case, which are only for adjudicating the present bail application.
16. With the above directions, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, in this Criminal Petition, shall stand closed.

___________ T. MALLIKARJUNA RAO, J.
Date: 18.12.2023.
